  "text": "Martin found his father in the shed, sorting screws into the lid of a biscuit tin.

“The kitchen drawer sticks,” his father said.

“You said it was the tap.”

“That too.”

Martin put his bag on the bench. There was a clean rectangle where the radio used to stand.

“Radio broken?”

“Couldn't get anything worth listening to.”

His father picked out two screws and put them in his shirt pocket.

Inside, the drawer came free with a jerk. Martin emptied it onto the table: string, takeaway menus, a torch without batteries.

“Don't throw those out.”

“The menus?”

“The elastic bands.”

Martin knelt and rubbed candle wax along the runners. His father stood beside him holding the drawer.

“Your mother used soap.”

“This lasts longer.”

“She had plenty of soap.”

They fitted the drawer back. His father opened it twice, then a third time with one finger.

“While you're here,” he said.

The tap needed a washer. Martin had brought the wrong size.

“Shop shuts at twelve,” his father said.

“It's ten past.”

“Tomorrow, then.”

Martin began putting the tools away.

“I can come Saturday.”

His father gathered the elastic bands, stretching each between his fingers before returning it to the drawer.

“Saturday's all right.”

At the door, he handed Martin the radio in a shopping bag.

“Have a look, if you've time.”

Martin felt its weight settle against his leg.

“Have you tried new batteries?”

His father reached into his shirt pocket and took out the two screws.

“Give me those here,” he said."
